session_1758608709025_rwryysw: To what extent do you support or oppose universal healthcare policies that provide government-funded healthcare coverage for all citizens? Please explain your reasoning.
column3: I absolutely support universal healthcare policy. Healthcare should be a human right. It shouldn't depend on your income or the color of your skin or your pre-existing conditions.

session_1758608709025_rwryysw: What do you think are the most significant impacts, positive or negative, of implementing a universal healthcare system?
column3: The most significant impacts are positive and that everyone would have health care. You wouldn't have to decide between, you know, paying your rent or getting your medication.

session_1758608709025_rwryysw: How do you think universal healthcare policies might affect healthcare quality and accessibility?
column3: I don't think it would really affect quality or accessibility.

session_1758608709025_rwryysw: What impact do you believe a universal healthcare system might have on medical innovation and research?
column3: If anything, it might improve medical innovation and research, is that if more people were able to get the health care they needed, there would be more data for researchers to look at.

session_1758608709025_rwryysw: How do you think universal healthcare might affect the economic burden on individuals and families?
column3: It would lessen the burden. People would be able to have insurance if they need any kind of health care instead of having to go to the hospital in a crisis and come home with a bill that is hundreds of thousands of dollars and they can never pay in their lifetime.

session_1758608709025_rwryysw: What role do you believe government should play in healthcare delivery and financing?
column3: I believe government will have to step in and help regulate things because unfortunately our healthcare system, big pharma companies, it's all for profit. So the government would have to step in and do something.

session_1758608709025_rwryysw: How might healthcare provider concerns factor into decisions about universal healthcare implementation?
column3: I don't think health care provider concerns are a factor. I don't believe that the majority of health care providers get into it for the money. It is definitely a calling and I believe they do it for the most part because they want to help others.

session_1758608709025_rwryysw: What economic effects, both positive and negative, might result from transitioning to a universal healthcare system?
column3: I believe there would be positive economic effects if everyone had health care, because now there are a lot of people that use an emergency room for their doctor, and then if they can't pay it off, the health care facility or the hospital has to write those charges off, and then everything else goes up to compensate for it. So I think it would have a positive economic effect, a strong positive economic effect.

session_1758608709025_rwryysw: How do you think the interests of taxpayers versus healthcare consumers should be balanced when making healthcare policy?
column3: I think taxes should be raised a little bit if it means everyone has health care.

session_1758608709025_rwryysw: What role do you think social equity and access to care play in discussions about healthcare policy?
column3: I think it's socially equitable for everyone to have access to health care.

session_1758608709025_rwryysw: Is the effect of Healthcare as a human right on Support for universal healthcare immediate, or does it take time to develop? Does it have a positive effect (increasing it) or a negative effect (decreasing it)? How strong is this effect?
column3: If everyone was allowed to have health care as a human right, the effect would be immediate. I think it would be a strong positive effect and it would be immediate.

session_1758608709025_rwryysw: What might lead to increases or decreases in Support for universal healthcare, and how significant are these effects? Please also indicate if these influences are positive (increasing) or negative (decreasing).
column3: Decreases in support can be, I suppose, for selfish people who feel that, you know, they only have to take care of themselves. They don't have to worry about society or community as a whole.

session_1758608709025_rwryysw: How confident are you that changes in Access to healthcare lead to changes in Support for universal healthcare? Does it have a positive effect (increasing it) or a negative effect (decreasing it)? How strong is this effect?
column3: I believe that changes in access to health care is a positive effect in supporting universal health care, then everyone would be able to have access to health care.

column3: Positive impacts of universal health care would lead to support for universal health care. Usually positive impacts lead to more support.

column3: Support for universal health care would increase with changes to health care quality, everyone would be able to have health care, so I would imagine that would support people's opinions for universal health care?

column3: The economic burden would be immediate and it would be strong if someone had insurance that would cover their medication that they can't afford to pay every month that would be an immediate economic effect.
